candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Karpathy-Inspired Claude Code Guidelines

> Check out my new project [Multica](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica) — an open-source platform for running and managing coding agents with reusable skills.
>
> Follow me on X: [https://x.com/jiayuan_jy](https://x.com/jiayuan_jy)

A single `CLAUDE.md` file to improve Claude Code behavior, derived from [Andrej Karpathy's observations](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2015883857489522876) on LLM coding pitfalls.

English | [简体中文](./README.zh.md)

## The Problems

From Andrej's post:

> "The models make wrong assumptions on your behalf and just run along with them without checking. They don't manage their confusion, don't seek clarifications, don't surface inconsistencies, don't present tradeoffs, don't push back when they should."

> "They really like to overcomplicate code and APIs, bloat abstractions, don't clean up dead code... implement a bloated construction over 1000 lines when 100 would do."

> "They still sometimes change/remove comments and code they don't sufficiently understand as side effects, even if orthogonal to the task."

## The Solution

Four principles in one file that directly address these issues:

| Principle | Addresses |
|-----------|-----------|
| **Think Before Coding** | Wrong assumptions, hidden confusion, missing tradeoffs |
| **Simplicity First** | Overcomplication, bloated abstractions |
| **Surgical Changes** | Orthogonal edits, touching code you shouldn't |
| **Goal-Driven Execution** | Leverage through tests-first, verifiable success criteria |

## The Four Principles in Detail

### 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

LLMs often pick an interpretation silently and run with it. This principle forces explicit reasoning:

- **State assumptions explicitly** — If uncertain, ask rather than guess
- **Present multiple interpretations** — Don't pick silently when ambiguity exists
- **Push back when warranted** — If a simpler approach exists, say so
- **Stop when confused** — Name what's unclear and ask for clarification

### 2. Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

Combat the tendency toward overengineering:

- No features beyond what was asked
- No abstractions for single-use code
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested
- No error handling for impossible scenarios
- If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite it

**The test:** Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated? If y

# DubWorld

English · [Türkçe](README.tr.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [Français](README.fr.md) · [العربية](README.ar.md) · [Português (BR)](README.pt-BR.md) · [Italiano](README.it.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [हिन्दी](README.hi.md) · [Bahasa Indonesia](README.id.md) · [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md) · [Polski](README.pl.md) · [Nederlands](README.nl.md) · [Українська](README.uk.md) · [فارسی](README.fa.md) · [עברית](README.he.md) · [ไทย](README.th.md) · [বাংলা](README.bn.md) · [اردو](README.ur.md) · [Ελληνικά](README.el.md) · [Čeština](README.cs.md) · [Română](README.ro.md) · [Magyar](README.hu.md) · [Svenska](README.sv.md) · [Azərbaycanca](README.az.md) · [Bahasa Melayu](README.ms.md)

> DubWorld dubs a video into another language on your own computer: speech to text with word timestamps, translation, synthetic voice kept in step with the original video (speech sped up at most 1.25×, the picture retimed for the rest), subtitles and a new video. Turkish by default; other languages per voice engine ([docs/diller.md](docs/diller.md)).

## Let your AI assistant install it

No programming needed. Open an AI assistant that can run commands on your computer (Claude Code, Codex,
Gemini CLI or similar) and paste this one sentence:

```text
Install the video dubbing program from https://github.com/alexturkey/DubWorld on this computer. Follow the AGENTS.md file in that repository step by step, detect my hardware yourself and do not ask me technical questions. When `dubla kontrol` says READY and the sample dub works, open the program's window for me.
```

The assistant measures your computer (graphics card, processor, memory, disk) and asks you once, in plain words, what
kind of setup you want: quick, recommended for your computer, or full. It explains each part (what it does, its disk
space, time and license) and asks whether you accept the terms of use of the parts you choose, starting with the
default voice. Then it installs, makes a sample dub and opens the program window. First steps, plain words and common
problems: **[docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md)**.

**License box:** code Apache-2.0. Default models: Supertonic 3 voice under OpenRAIL-M (use restrictions, accepted once); Opus-MT and the Turkish word-timing model under CC BY 4.0 (attribution, NOTICE); FFmpeg build GPL-3.0 (separate program). Non-commercial only and off by default: CrisperWhisper 2.0

# OpenBot

[![CI](https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm_Noncommercial_1.0.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. It supports the local
[Codex App Server](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server) and
[Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview), plus [Grok CLI](https://docs.x.ai/build/overview),
OpenCode, Gemini, [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli), and [Cline CLI](https://cline.bot/cli) through ACP. It gives every agent its own workspace and
conversation, and provides local queues, file transfers, an embedded browser, and agent-to-agent
messaging in one desktop app.

> [!WARNING]
> OpenBot is a development preview. Agents currently run with `danger-full-access` and
> `approvalPolicy: never`. They can read and modify files, run commands, use the network, and control
> the embedded browser without per-action confirmations after the explicit first-launch consent.
> Run only agents and tasks you trust, keep backups, and review [Security](#security) before use.

## What works

- Prompt-driven agent creation and editing on desktop and mobile, with editable instructions, avatar, and section review before saving.
- Persistent agents backed by independent Codex, Claude, Grok, OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor, or Cline sessions and local workspaces.
- Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints and custom ACP agents, with detection of local model servers (Ollama, LM Studio) and installed agents.
- Per-agent context monitoring with automatic compaction before long threads exhaust the model window.
- FIFO message queues with pause, resume, cancellation, and crash-safe persistence.
- Agent-to-agent messages, replies, reactions, images, and managed file transfers.
- Shared desktop channel chats with one task owner, explicit delegation, shared history, and Stop, Resume, Reassign, Archive, and Restore controls.
- A persistent embedded browser that agents can open, inspect, and control.
- Optional Computer Use on macOS, Windows and Linux through the `cua-driver` binary in the release, which OpenBot starts as its own child process and gives to every provider.
- Per-agent model, reasoning, profile, notification, browser, and panel state.
- Local data and privacy-safe diagnostics exports from the account menu.
- Optional OpenBot accounts through one-time email cod

candidates.description: macOS app: drop a podcast or video, get a transcript with every line assigned to a speaker. On-device, built on Desert Ant Labs' Who + Apple's speech transcriber.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Who Said What

A small macOS app that turns a podcast, interview or meeting recording into a transcript where every line is assigned to a speaker. Drop an audio or video file on the window and you get a speaker timeline, a clickable transcript and exports for subtitles and show notes. Everything runs on your Mac. No audio is uploaded.

![Who Said What: drop a podcast, watch both models run, get a speaker-labelled transcript](docs/demo.gif)

It's built on [**Who**](https://desertant.com/models/who/), the on-device speaker diarization model from [Desert Ant Labs](https://desertant.com/), paired with Apple's built-in speech transcriber.

## How it works

Who works out *who spoke when*: it returns numbered speaker turns with start and end times. It doesn't transcribe and doesn't know anyone's name. To get "who said what", the app runs two on-device models at the same time:

| Step | Model | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who spoke when | **Who** (Swift SDK [`desert-ant-core`](https://github.com/Desert-Ant-Labs/desert-ant-core) 4.1, `Who` product) | Speaker turns: `speaker`, `start`, `end` |
| What was said | **Apple `SpeechTranscriber`** (Speech framework, macOS 26) | Words with timestamps |

Each word goes to the speaker turn it overlaps most; a word in a gap goes to the nearest turn. Consecutive words from the same speaker become one paragraph.

## Features

- **Drop zone** or a "Choose File…" button. Takes WAV, MP3, M4A, AIFF, MP4 and MOV.
- **Live progress** with a running timer and two progress bars (Who labelling speakers, and transcription), each with a live "× realtime" figure.
- **Speed tiles** on the results screen for Who, speech to text and the whole pipeline.
- **Speaker timeline**: one coloured lane per speaker. Click anywhere to jump there.
- **Transcript**: click a line to play from that point. The line being played is highlighted and scrolls into view.
- **Video panel** for video files: the border takes the current speaker's colour and their name shows in the corner.
- **Rename speakers**: click a speaker chip or a name in the transcript, type a name and press Return. Names show up everywhere, including exports.
- **Export** (⌘E) with your speaker names:

  | Format | Looks like | Good for |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Text with timecodes (`.txt`) | `[00:01:23] Name: what they said` | Show notes, reading, docs |
  | Subtitles (`.srt`) | `Name: what they said`, short cues | YouTube, Premiere, Final Cut, DaVinci |

# WebKit

WebKit is a cross-platform web browser engine. On iOS and macOS, it powers Safari, Mail, Apple Books, and many other applications. For more information about WebKit, see the [WebKit project website](https://webkit.org/).

## Trying the Latest

On macOS, [download Safari Technology Preview](https://webkit.org/downloads/) to test the latest version of WebKit. On Linux, download [Epiphany Technology Preview](https://webkitgtk.org/epiphany-tech-preview). On Windows, you'll have to build it yourself.

## Reporting Bugs

1. [Search WebKit Bugzilla](https://bugs.webkit.org/query.cgi?format=specific&product=WebKit) to see if there is an existing report for the bug you've encountered.
2. [Create a Bugzilla account](https://bugs.webkit.org/createaccount.cgi) to report bugs (and comment on them) if you haven't done so already.
3. File a bug in accordance with [our guidelines](https://webkit.org/bug-report-guidelines/).

Once your bug is filed, you will receive email when it is updated at each stage in the [bug life cycle](https://webkit.org/bug-life-cycle). After the bug is considered fixed, you may be asked to download the [latest nightly](https://webkit.org/nightly) and confirm that the fix works for you.

## Getting the Code

Run the following command to clone WebKit's Git repository:

```
git clone https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit.git WebKit
```

You can enable [git fsmonitor](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-corefsmonitor) to make many git commands faster (such as `git status`) with `git config core.fsmonitor true`

## Building WebKit

### Building for Apple platforms

Install Xcode and its command line tools if you haven't done so already:

1. **Install Xcode**
2. **Install the Xcode Command Line Tools** In Terminal, run the command: `xcode-select --install`
3. **Install the Metal toolchain** In Terminal, run the command: `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`

Run the following command to build a macOS debug build with debugging symbols and assertions:

```
Tools/Scripts/build-webkit --debug
```

For performance testing, and other purposes, use `--release` instead. If you
also need debug symbols (dSYMs), run:

```
Tools/Scripts/build-webkit --release DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT=dwarf-with-dsym 
```

To build for an embedded platform like iOS, tvOS, or watchOS, pass a platform
argument to `build-webkit`.

candidates.readme_excerpt: **Give the agent you already use a memory you control.** GBrain stores explicit facts with their sources, supports corrections and withdrawal, and makes the same memory available across your agents. Start with keyless memory and keyword retrieval; add semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment when you need them. > [!TIP] > **Need hosted? First time running an agent?** Try **[gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=readme)**, hosted GBrain, for the easiest experience: one brain for you and your team, connected to ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor, with nothing to install or keep online. Stuck? Email support@gbrain.io and a person will set it up with you, free. **Keep skills beside knowledge.** New local brains include memory skills in their content root. Agents can join an authorized catalog; only approved editors can publish. Managed coding-agent installs add an owned native router; restart and real-use verification are separate steps. Staged migration preserves sharing choices and personal edits. See [shared brain skills](docs/guides/shared-brain-skills.md). ## Choose your setup 1. **Add GBrain to my existing agent — recommended.** Keep your agent's identity and save memory inside its environment. # ex-USSR Kinship Research

![ex-USSR Kinship Research cover](docs/cover.jpg)

**An evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code and other Agent Skills runtimes).** It turns an agent into a careful family-history researcher for the former USSR, the Soviet Union and the Russian Empire. The agent reads church books and civil records, military, deportation and repression files, and unindexed archive scans. It keeps every find traceable, separates records from interpretation and says plainly what is proven and what is not.

Coverage includes all 15 former Soviet republics: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Archives are chosen by the event's historical jurisdiction and current record custodian; a regional example does not replace local research.

The skill's instructions are written in Russian, but **the agent talks to you in your language**: English, Ukrainian, Russian, Polish, German and so on. It quotes sources in their original spelling with a translation, and builds search queries in the languages of the records.

---

- **Case intake and scope.** One research question, known facts, who may be alive, what is off-limits.

- **Name-variant matrices.** Pre-reform Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Romanian, German and Yiddish forms, patronymics, maiden names and transliterations.
- **Source strategy.** Originals first, then official catalogs, indexes, published document collections, and only then trees and forums as leads.

- **Identity resolution.** Namesakes stay separate `person_id`s until distinguishing evidence appears: house number, parents, godparents, exact birth date or military unit.

# tstack

The agent skills I use every day, cleaned up so anyone can use them. They work
in Claude Code and Codex. Some use [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code)
features when they are available and fall back to native tools when they are
not.

## Skills

| Skill | Say | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `full-send` | "full send" | Takes a change to a merged PR with nobody watching: proves it, reviews it, files it, babysits it, merges it. |
| `full-stop` | "full stop" | Same as `full-send`, but stops when the PR is ready for you to merge. |
| `council` | "council" | Gets review from three models from different providers, and loops until they agree. |
| `sol-loop` | "sol loop" | Reviews a change with GPT Sol in a loop until both agents agree. |
| `file-pr` | "file a PR" | Files a short PR that leads with the problem, not an inventory of changes. |
| `takeover` | "take over" | Finishes someone else's PR, branch, or agent thread, and keeps their credit. |
| `babysit-pr` | "babysit" | Watches a PR through CI and review bots, and fixes the real findings. |
| `modernize` | "modernize" | Rebases an old PR and decides if it should still exist. |
| `leaving-pr-comments` | (automatic) | Formats comments that an agent posts on your behalf. |

Some skills call others. Install the ones they need too:

- `full-send` uses `sol-loop`, `file-pr`, and `babysit-pr`.
- `full-stop` uses `full-send`.
- `takeover` uses `modernize`, `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `leaving-pr-comments`.
- `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `modernize` use `leaving-pr-comments`.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/t3dotgg/tstack
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/   # Claude Code
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.codex/skills/    # Codex
```

## Requirements

- An authenticated [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh`).
- `python3` for `babysit-pr`'s `pr-wait` script.
- `council` and `sol-loop` need subagents on other providers' models. T3 Code
  does this with `delegate_task`. Otherwise you need a harness that can run
  those models.

## Make them yours

These are starting points. Edit them. Put personal settings, like which models
sit on your council, in your `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, so you can update the
skills without losing them.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# agent-purge

一份系统提示词，喂给多个 coding agent。支持替换（replace）、只发人设（strict）、追加（append）、清空（off）四种模式，可热切换，全程可逆。

```
agent-purge web          # 本地控制台 http://127.0.0.1:7788
agent-purge codex        # 用当前 persona 启动 codex
agent-purge pi --ask "…" # 一次性提问
```

## 它做什么

每家 coding agent 读系统提示词的位置都不一样：有的认启动参数，有的认配置文件，有的只能靠插件改运行时对象。agent-purge 把这些入口统一成三件事：

| 通道 | 机制 | 生效范围 |
|---|---|---|
| `install` | 写入该 harness 的托管配置块（Markdown / hooks / 插件） | 常驻，别人启动也生效 |
| `shim` | 往 PATH 前置同名小壳，转发给 `agent-purge <h>` | 裸敲命令也接管 |
| `slash` | 会话内 `/purge on\|off\|status` | 热切换，不动磁盘 |

三层都写的是同一份 `personas/<id>.md` 的正文。`--mode off` 或 Web 总开关关掉时，全部撤回到原样——不留残渣。

## 安装

```bash
npm i -g agent-purge     # 或 npx agent-purge web
```

要求 Node ≥ 20，零依赖。

**数据独立存放**，升级不会被覆盖：默认 `~/.agent-purge/`（Windows `C:\Users\<你>\.agent-purge\`），里面是 `state.json` 和 `personas/`。想换位置就设环境变量：

```bash
export AGENT_PURGE_HOME=/path/to/your/data     # Windows: setx AGENT_PURGE_HOME D:\ap-data
```

旧版本（0.1.x）把数据放在包目录里，首次运行会自动搬到新家，原文件不动。

## 人设

`personas/<id>.md` = frontmatter + 正文。正文就是会被写进系统提示词的那一段。

frontmatter 用 `description` 写「说明」（Web 列表和 `agent-purge ls` 显示的就是它）；旧的 `desc` 仍然认，不会报错。可选 `order`（排序）、`harness` / `model`（匹配用）。Web 里只改名字和说明时会保留 frontmatter 的其它键，不整段重写。

```bash
agent-purge ls                 # 列出全部 persona，标出当前匹配的
agent-purge use <id>           # 切换当前 persona
agent-purge pi --persona <id>  # 只这一轮用别的
```

首次运行会在 `personas/` 下生成 `neutral.md` 起步模板。

## 支持情况

`agent-purge ls` 和 Web 控制台显示的是**运行期真值**：每个 harness 有没有装、版本、注入层（SYS / USER）、三个通道各自可用性。`matrix.json` 里是静态能力表，两者冲突时以运行期为准。

闭源桌面端（提示词在服务端或二进制里）只做原样启动，不做任何注入——`agent-purge <h>` 会明确打印原因，不会假装生效。

## magpie 网关插件（可选）

[magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie) 把各家 agent 的请求收进本地网关。挂上这个插件后，**凡是经过网关的请求**（Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode、pi…）的 system 段都按 agent-purge 的当前人设改写——不用逐个 harness 装，换人设也不用重启 magpie。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ZiChuanLan/agent-purge
```

# ai-wallet-binance

让你的 AI 用你自己的币安 AI 钱包交易。

跟 Claude、Codex、DeepSeek 或 Grok 说一句“这个币买 0.05 BNB”，它就用你的币安 Agentic Wallet 去买，包括只有带
Agent ID 的 AI 钱包才能买的新币。私钥在币安手里，每笔交易都由币安签名；本工具碰不到私钥，在你自己的电脑或服务器上运行。

中文 | [English](https://github.com/jacke-pp/ai-wallet-binance/blob/main/README_en.md)

## 能做什么

- **按合约地址买卖**：Four.meme Agent 币、Flap ID Agent Curve 币、GANG 发射台、Flap 内盘、PancakeSwap。
- **狙击**：盯一个币（按创建者、名字或时间）开盘就买；或者抢某个发射台上最先出来的几个 Agent 新币。每个币买多少、
  买几个、每天最多花多少、能接受多高的税，都由你定，没有默认值。
- **买前检查**：币安公开的代币安全检测，加上用你自己的钱包地址在链上模拟“买一点再全卖掉”，隐藏税和卖不掉的币在花钱前就能看出来。
- **Mint**：包括只有 AI 钱包能 mint 的 NFT。给它合约地址和每个最多付多少，它自己找 mint 函数和价格，先模拟确认 NFT
  真的能到账才发；预售没开可以守着等。
- **自己调设置**：滑点、gas 上限、交易卡住自动加速、花费上限、最高买入税和卖出税。税率是用你自己的钱包地址模拟买卖实测出来的，不只看合约写的。
- **记账**：每笔交易和盈亏都记在你自己电脑上。
- **在浏览器里点着交易**：不想打字就运行 `aiwb ui`，在你自己电脑上打开一个交易页面。首页是“战壕”三列：新创建、
  即将打满、已开盘（Four、Flap、GANG 三个平台的 Agent 币），每张卡片有内盘进度、税、市值、持有人数和快买按钮（金额自己填）。
  点进一个币有实时 K 线、买前检查、一键买卖、领取，还有持仓和狙击。
- **领完或毕业后自动转出**：可选。设好你的地址，再分别打开 Flap（发币后自动领币再转出）、Four（毕业后转出）、GANG
  （毕业后转出）的开关，币一能动就全部转到你的地址。默认全关；只转打开以后买到的币，每个币只转一次，失败会自动重试。
  也可以手动转：`aiwb send <币> <地址>`。
- **接 GMGN 数据（只读）**：填上你自己的 GMGN API key，交易页面的 K 线和持仓分布、前 10 持仓、创建者持仓、新钱包、
  机器人、流动性、合约权限就从 GMGN 来；AI 也能用 `aiwb gmgn` 查。下单仍走币安 AI 钱包：GMGN 的钱包没有 Agent ID，
  买不了 Agent 专属币。

## 开始

需要 Node.js 18 以上，和开好 AI 钱包的币安 App。

```bash
npm install -g @binance/agentic-wallet
npm install -g ai-wallet-binance
aiwb doctor
```

然后跟你的 AI 说：“运行 `aiwb agents`，读完它打印的说明，帮我设置好”。它会运行 `aiwb login`，给你一个链接去币安 App
里确认，再告诉你 App 里要打开哪些设置（Agent ID、开发者模式）。（`aiwb agents --path` 会显示说明文件在哪。）

也可以不用 AI，直接运行 `aiwb ui`：浏览器打开交易页面并显示二维码，用币安 App 扫码登录。页面只在你自己电脑上运行
（127.0.0.1），只认它打印出来的那个链接。钥匙一直在币安，每笔交易都由币安签名。

在币安 App 的 AI 钱包设置里，把**异常交易处理**改成在 App 内确认。币安审计评为有风险的币（目前 GANG
发射台内盘的币都是，合约没开源），每笔交易都会被判成有风险：设成自动拒绝就会失败，设成 App 确认就会推到你手机上，
点一下确认就成交。买之前 `aiwb check` 和交易页面会提示这个币卖出要不要点确认。

## 怎么跟它说

| 你说 | 它运行 |
|---|---|
| “0x... 安全吗？” | `aiwb check 0x...` |
| “0x... 买 0.05 BNB” | `aiwb buy 0x... 0.05` |
| “卖一半” | `aiwb sell 0x... 50%` |
| “狙 Four 的 Agent 新币，每个 0.02，最多 3 个” | 先问你每天上限和最高税，再 `aiwb snipe add watch ...` |
| “我赚了多少？” | `aiwb pnl` |
| “打开交易页面” | `aiwb ui` |
| “把 0x... 全部转到 0x...” | 先跟你核对币、数量和地址，再 `aiwb send 0x... 0x...` |
| “毕业后自动转到我的地址 0x...” | `aiwb config set autoSendTo 0x...`，再打开 `autoSendFour` / `autoSendGang` / `autoSendFlap` |
| “看 0x... 的 GMGN 持仓” | `aiwb gmgn holders 0x...` |

## 用之前要知道

- Agent 币还在只限 AI 钱包的内盘阶段时，币安可能不让 AI 钱包卖出。做好拿到它上 PancakeSwap 的准备，只买你拿得住的量。
- 每笔交易币安都会先检查再签名，可能拒绝。每日限额和风控设置在 App 里，不在这里。
- 自动转出只在 `aiwb ui` 开着（或运行 `aiwb a
